questions.prompt: Which organelle releases energy from glucose?
Where are proteins made in a cell?
questions.explain: Ribosomes assemble proteins using instructions from DNA.

questions.prompt: Which organelle is called the “suicide bag” of the cell?
questions.explain: Its enzymes can digest the cell itself if it is badly damaged.

questions.prompt: Which three structures are found in plant cells but not animal cells?
options: Cell wall, chloroplasts and a large vacuole
questions.explain: Both kinds of cell share the rest.

questions.prompt: Match each organelle to its job.
questions.explain: Each organelle has a specific job.

questions.prompt: Cells in the pancreas make and release large amounts of digestive enzymes (proteins). Which organelles would they have a lot of?
questions.explain: Rough ER makes and transports proteins; the Golgi packages them for export.

questions.prompt: What is the difference between the cell wall and the cell membrane?
options: The wall is rigid and supports; the membrane is flexible and controls entry and exit
The wall controls what enters; the membrane gives support
Only animal cells have a membrane
questions.explain: The cellulose wall is fully permeable; the membrane is partially permeable.

questions.prompt: Sperm cells swim a long way and contain many mitochondria. Explain the link between their structure and function.
questions.modelAnswer: Swimming needs a lot of energy. Mitochondria carry out respiration, releasing energy from glucose. Having many mitochondria (packed in the middle piece near the tail) lets the sperm release enough energy to beat its tail and swim to the egg.
rubric: More mitochondria = more energy for the tail
